_meta.indication: AMPYRA (dalfampridine) is indicated to improve walking in patients with multiple sclerosis (MS), demonstrated by an increase in walking speed

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel group, double-blind 21-week study (14-week double-blind treatment) at 33 centers in the U.S. and Canada
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with multiple sclerosis able to walk 25 feet in 8-45 seconds; excluded history of seizures or epileptiform EEG activity
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Timed-Walk Response (consistent improvement in walking speed on the Timed 25-Foot Walk, responder analysis)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel group, double-blind 14-week study (9 weeks double-blind treatment) at 39 centers in the U.S. and Canada
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with multiple sclerosis using the same inclusion/exclusion criteria as Trial 1, additionally excluding severe renal impairment
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Timed-Walk Response (consistent improvement in walking speed on the Timed 25-Foot Walk, responder analysis)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=2% and more than placebo) included urinary tract infection (12% vs 8% placebo), insomnia (9% vs 4%), dizziness (7% vs 4%), headache (7% vs 4%), and nausea (7% vs 3%); the primary safety concern was dose-related seizures
target_moa: Broad spectrum potassium channel blocker that increases conduction of action potentials in demyelinated axons through inhibition of potassium channels

rems.type: A REMS was required to ensure the benefits outweigh the risk of seizures, consisting of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments

advisory_committee.vote: The Peripheral and Central Nervous Systems (PCNS) Advisory Committee on October 14, 2009 voted 12-1 that the data provide substantial evidence of effectiveness

summary.text: Traditional approval of a new molecular entity (dalfampridine, 4-aminopyridine) based on two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials (MS-F203 and MS-F204) demonstrating improved walking speed; reviewed by the PCNS Advisory Committee which voted 12-1 for substantial evidence of effectiveness; approved with a REMS (Medication Guide and communication plan) to address the seizure risk.

citations.quote: The two pivotal Phase 3 studies (MS-F203 and MS-F204) were parallel group, randomized, double-blind study comparing Fampridine-SR 10 mg b.i.d. with placebo.
The Committee voted 12-1 that the data provide substantial evidence of effectiveness for fampridine as a treatment to improve walking in patients with MS.
In accordance with section 505-1 of FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for AMPYRA (dalfampridine) to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risk of seizures.
